We'll explore what it means to be an engineer, systems thinking, problem framing, and much more.
Let's begin with understanding how the course works and what you can expect.
This study guide is designed to be your companion throughout the course.
It contains course maps, sources, key points, questions with model answers, glossaries, and consolidated references.
The guide is structured by weeks, making it easy to follow along with your coursework.
In Week 1, we'll explore what it means to be an engineer as a profession.
We'll discuss the key points, ethical codes including the NSPE codes, and personal ethics.
You'll also find lecture and lab questions with model answers, textbook assignments, and a glossary of terms.
Week 1 introduces you to the fundamental aspects of engineering as a profession.
You'll learn about professional responsibilities and duties that come with being an engineer.
We'll explore the engineering code of ethics, which provides guidelines for ethical behavior.
Specifically, we'll examine the NSPE codes and how they apply to real engineering situations.

data.heading: Week 1 Ethics: NSPE Codes and Personal Ethics
bullets: NSPE Code of Ethics for Engineers

narr: A crucial part of Week 1 is understanding the ethical framework that guides engineering practice.
The NSPE Code of Ethics for Engineers provides a comprehensive set of guidelines.
The code includes Fundamental Canons that establish the basic principles.
It also contains Rules of Practice that provide more specific guidance.
Professional Obligations outline what engineers owe to their profession and society.
We'll develop a framework for ethical decision-making that you can apply throughout your career.

data.title: Week 2
data.subtitle: Systems Thinking I: Systems, Boundaries, Stakeholders

narr: In Week 2, we dive into systems thinking, which is fundamental to engineering.
We'll learn how to identify systems, define their boundaries, and identify stakeholders.
Understanding these concepts will help you approach engineering problems more effectively.

data.heading: Key Points of Week 2
bullets: Applying systems thinking to engineering problems

narr: Week 2 focuses on systems thinking, a critical approach in engineering.
You'll learn what constitutes a system and how to identify its components.
We'll explore how to define system boundaries, which separate what's included from what's not.
Recognizing stakeholders and understanding their interests is another key skill you'll develop.
The systems thinking methodology provides a structured approach to problem-solving.
Finally, you'll apply these concepts to real engineering problems.

data.title: Week 3
data.subtitle: Systems Thinking II: Process Flow Diagrams (PFD)

narr: Week 3 builds on your systems thinking foundation by introducing process flow diagrams.
PFDs are essential tools for visualizing and understanding engineering processes.
You'll learn how to create and interpret these diagrams effectively.

data.heading: Key Points of Week 3
bullets: Process flow diagram components and symbols

narr: Week 3 introduces process flow diagrams, or PFDs, which are vital in engineering.
You'll learn about the components and symbols used in PFDs.
We'll cover how to create effective PFDs that clearly represent processes.
Interpreting PFDs for system analysis is another key skill you'll develop.
Mass balance principles are fundamental to understanding process flows.
Finally, you'll apply PFDs to solve engineering problems.

parts.note: Material used up within the system
Change in material within the system over time

narr: A fundamental equation in engineering is the mass balance formula.
The input represents all material entering the system.
The output represents all material leaving the system.
Generation refers to material created within the system.
Consumption refers to material used up within the system.
Accumulation is the change in material within the system over time.
Week 4 introduces problem framing and modeling, essential skills for engineers.
You'll learn how to properly frame engineering problems and develop appropriate models.
These skills will help you approach complex engineering challenges systematically.

Finally, you'll apply these concepts to various engineering scenarios.
